The precise statements are in its 2 constituent manuscript(s): Primitive roots for every admissible integer base (preprints/Primitive-roots-for-every-admissible-integer-base-October-4-2026/primitive-roots-all-integer-bases.pdf); Simultaneous primitive roots: a conditional lower bound for prime bases (preprints/Simultaneous-primitive-roots-a-conditional-lower-bound-for-prime-bases-October-4-2026/simultaneous-primitive-roots-conditional-lower-bound-prime-bases.pdf). AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base. Proves the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture for every integer a that is neither −1 nor a square. For each such base, at least $`c_a x/(\log x)^2`$ primes in every sufficiently large interval $`(x,2x)`$ have primitive root a, with $`c_a\gt 0`$.
